data.name: Radharaman
data.gender_notes: Radharaman is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Radharaman is a compound name derived from Sanskrit. Radha refers to the Goddess of Love and Rama means God. Thus, Radharaman signifies God of Love. The name Radharaman carries the meaning “God of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Radharaman usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Radharaman is a revered name in Hinduism. It is believed that invoking this name can bring blessings of love and happiness in life.
data.etymology: Radharaman belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Radharaman total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Radharaman holds immense significance in Hindu culture, especially in eastern India and Nepal, where traditions like Vaishnavism and Gaudiya Vaishnavism are popular. Radharaman or Radha-Rama signifies the divine couple, Radha and Krishna, who represent the eternal frolic between love (Radha), longing (Krishna), and the fulfilment of that love. Radharaman is believed to be an incarnation of this divine amour, embodying the sacred bond of love and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Radharaman represents the ultimate goal of every soul- union with the supreme divinity. The love between Radha and Krishna is a reflection of the longing and the divine connection of each soul with the Almighty. The name imbues its bearer with a deep sense of love for God, fani (mythical soulful love), devotion, and commitment, inspiring them to always seek the divine presence. In turn, the auspicious name is believed to bestow its owner with spiritual blessings and harmonious blessings, ensuring a fulfilling and rich life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Radharaman symbolizes the divine union of Radha and Krishna, embodying the essence of unconditional love and devotion. This name is a reminder of the ultimate reality, where the individual soul merges with the infinite divine consciousness.

historical_references.reference: Radharaman, a name for Lord Vishnu, is mentioned in the Puranas, particularly the Padma Purana. It is one of the 21 grand names of Vishnu, and is described as the one who has Radha in his heart.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a collection of Hindu scriptures that describe the history and legends of the gods and heroes. They were composed between the 4th and 8th centuries CE, and provide insights into the religious and cultural practices of ancient India.

historical_references.reference: The temple town of Radharaman, in Madhya Pradesh, India, was named after Lord Vishnu in this form. The temple, which dates back to the 16th century, is famous for its intricately carved marble images of Radharaman, and is a major pilgrimage site for Hindus.
historical_references.context: Radharaman is a popular deity in the Hindu tradition, and several temples have been dedicated to him throughout India. The Radharaman temple in Madhya Pradesh is one of the most famous, and attracts millions of pilgrims every year.

trends: Devotional art, Modern Hinduism, Radha-Krishna iconography
modern_usage.modern_context: Radharaman is a name of Lord Krishna, specifically in the context of his divine association with Radha, a popular Hindu deity. In modern contexts, this name is often associated with Radha-Krishna iconography in Hindu devotional art. This depiction of Krishna as Radharaman is particularly popular in Bengal, India. The image of Radharaman shows Krishna holding the flute to his lips, with Radha standing beside him. This image is popularly shared on social media platforms like Instagram and Pinterest, as well as in physical art galleries.
